# P9-B1 — `TEMPLATE_DIFF`'s ceiling, published before its delta

**GENERATED by `tools/measure/p9_ceiling.py`. Run `make ceiling`.**

**G-EVAL: PASSED.** Every number on this page is derived from `cdfc.calc`; arm 2's oracle is LibreOffice Calc, recalculating the same workbook, INDEPENDENT.

## The headline

> **957 of the 3747 field-surface cells feed at least one formula the template declares.**

Per sheet: 3. Portfolio 400 · 4. Investors 368 · 5. PMS 104 · 1. Introduction 64 · 2. Summary 20 · 8. Compliance Status 1.

This is the **ceiling**, not the yield. Any claim that predicate #1 covers more than 957 cells is arithmetically impossible.

And the other half of the same measurement: **2790 field-surface cells feed no template formula at all.** They participate in no arithmetic relation the regulator encoded, so every recompute, carry and sum-identity check in the design is structurally blind to them, and only bound, membership and date predicates can reach them. That is a second, independent, measured argument that the residue set is non-empty — one that does not depend on the coordinated-misstatement construction at all.

## What a precedent is — three readings, and the count does not distinguish them

| reading | precedents | ceiling | formula cells binding ZERO field-surface cells |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `lexical` | every reference in the formula text | 957 | 115 |
| `value` | minus arguments read for their SHAPE only (`ROW`, `ROWS`, …) | 957 | 115 |
| `transitive` | followed THROUGH intermediate formula cells to the filer's inputs | 957 | 0 |

**All three agree on the ceiling and disagree about everything else.** The ceiling is a union, so it saturates; the per-cell binding is where the reading is decided. Under a direct reading **115 of the 505 formula cells bind nothing** and would be refused at G1 with `cells_bound = 0` — including `'1. Introduction'!D17`, the flagship's own worked example, whose direct precedents `D18:D20` are themselves formulas. Following through to `G54:G63` is not a widening: it is what `recalculate(..., formula_source="TEMPLATE")` actually does, since it recomputes the whole graph over the filed inputs.

**A count that agrees with a pin is evidence about the count.** Three readings returning 957 is the reason to trust 957; it is not a reason to think the reading did not matter.

## The eight cells the relation can never reach — MEASURED, and it corrects the plan

`plan/05` §0.1 records **8** cells that are unlocked *and* formula-bearing and calls a fixture overwriting one of them *"a strictly stronger demonstration and the one to show a reviewer"*, on the grounds that a filer needs no zip edit and no adversarial intent — **Excel alone will do it**. The first half is right. The conclusion is not, and the fixture is what showed it:

| overwritten cell | field surface | filing binds? | who catches it |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `'3. Portfolio'!O7` (locked) | 3747 → 3747 | yes | **`TEMPLATE_DIFF`** |
| `'4. Investors'!N5` (unlocked) | 3747 → 3748 | **no** | the template binder |

The field surface is *unlocked ∧ non-formula*, so deleting a formula from an **unlocked** cell moves that cell **into** the field surface. The structural fingerprint carries the unlocked mask, so the fingerprint moves, and the run terminates at F3 with `invalid.template_unbound` — five steps before the relation executes.

> **The claim that the fingerprint "excludes formula content" is false for exactly these 8 cells.** It excludes formula *text*; it does not exclude formula *presence*. This is §0.5's own mechanism — a catch credited to the wrong layer — reappearing inside P9's headline fixture, and it points the other way: the eight cells a filer can overwrite **without stripping protection** are the eight the flagship can never see.

The cells: `4. Investors!N14`, `4. Investors!N15`, `4. Investors!N16`, `4. Investors!N17`, `4. Investors!N5`, `4. Investors!N6`, `4. Investors!N7`, `4. Investors!N8`.

**So the ceiling has two numbers and both are published.** 957 of 3747 is the ceiling if every formula cell could be checked. **869 of 3747** is the ceiling over the 497 formula cells whose overwrite still binds — the flagship's real domain. The 88 cells in the difference are reachable only through a formula cell whose overwrite ends the run before the relation runs.

The remedy is named and is **not** taken here: making the fingerprint's mask style-only would restore all 505 cells to the relation, and it would move every template binding digest in the system. That is P5's binder, not P9's relation, and a phase that repairs another phase's load-bearing artifact as a side effect is how a build stops being re-derivable. Registered as NC-R11 with a guard, so it cannot be forgotten.

## Degree — who gets a tolerance, and on whose authority

`τ(n) = 5n` units of `MILLI_USD_MILLION` for degree 1; **0** for everything else. Of the 505 formula cells:

| basis | cells | degree |
|---|---:|---:|
| `MONEY_MARKER` | 223 | 1 |
| `RATIO_MARKER` | 115 | 0 |
| `COUNT_MARKER` | 93 | 0 |
| `NO_MARKER` | 72 | 0 |
| `DATE_MARKER` | 2 | 0 |

Every assignment names the regulator's own words and the cell they are in — `'1. Introduction'!D17` is degree 0 on the authority of `'1. Introduction'!C17`, *"Total No. of Schemes of the FME authorised by IFSCA"*. **A person, and a scheme, is not a rounded quantity**: under a blanket `τ(n) = 5n` that cell could be wrong by fifteen schemes and pass.

### TWO OPEN ITEMS IN THE HARVEST, dated 14 Aug 2026, found by building the degree map

Neither is repaired here, and the reason is the same for both: changing a harvested predicate's tolerance changes its envelope, therefore its `code_sha256`, therefore the registry root, therefore P7's funnel and P8's FFR. A phase that silently moves another phase's published numbers is how a build stops being re-derivable. Both are published, dated, and guarded so they cannot be forgotten.

**(a) `τ` is applied to counts.** **29 of the 79** harvested predicates that carry a tolerance carry it on a cell this degree map assigns degree 0. `harvest_classes/sum_identity.py` gives every `=SUM(range)` a `τ(n) = 5n` allowance without asking what the cells hold. That is NC-E08's defect standing in the harvest rather than in the probe layer.

Examples: `P-0007 at '1. Introduction'!D17 (COUNT_MARKER)`, `P-0220 at '3. Portfolio'!C167 (RATIO_MARKER)`, `P-0221 at '3. Portfolio'!D167 (RATIO_MARKER)`, `P-0222 at '3. Portfolio'!E167 (RATIO_MARKER)`, `P-0223 at '3. Portfolio'!F167 (RATIO_MARKER)`, `P-0224 at '3. Portfolio'!G167 (RATIO_MARKER)`.

**(b) Every emitted tolerance is 1,000× the one it was written to express, and this is the larger of the two.** `HALF_ULP = 5` is half a unit of `MILLI_USD_MILLION`, i.e. **0.005 USD Million**. `facts/fact_table.py` scales money to that unit — but only when given `money_keys`, and the runner does not use it. The tree the runner evaluates is `facts/build.py::fact_set_for`, whose `_coerce` returns the workbook's own number unscaled and says so in its own docstring: *"this builder does not know a cell's unit"*. So the literal in every emitted expression is a tolerance in **whole USD Million**.

Measured: the largest tolerance literal in the harvested set is **60**, and the distinct literals are [15, 20, 50, 55, 60]. Worked instance — `P-0114` over `'3. Portfolio'!O7`:

```
filing.n_3_portfolio.r7.co.v - (…twelve summands…) <= 60
```

On the reference clean filing that row's twelve summands are `1` each and the total is `12`. **The check passes for any total between −48 and 72.** The tolerance it was written to express is 0.06 USD Million.

This is a measurement error correlated with the quantity being measured, in the direction that flatters us: an arithmetic mutant smaller than the over-wide tolerance is `WRONG`, observable, and **not killed** — so it depresses `K/O` rather than inflating it. The sign matters and it is the reason this is an open item rather than an emergency: the published kill rate is a LOWER bound on what these predicates can do, not an upper one.

Guarded by `tests/negative/test_nc_probes.py::test_nc__R12a_the_tolerance_unit_mismatch_is_still_open`, which fails the day either side is repaired without the other — because a scaled fact tree with unscaled literals, or the reverse, is the same defect with the sign flipped.
